ThisIsTea teaches you to spot scams with short lessons and practice. It is a free learning project made at LauzHack 2026. By using it, you agree to these terms.

We store your email address, your name, your answers and your progress, to teach you and to keep your progress safe. For the password you choose, we keep a few facts (like its length and whether it appears in known data breaches) for your password lesson, never the password itself. We keep a short list of device settings (like dark mode, text size and time zone) to adapt the app. We do not read your contacts and we do not track you on other sites. The page What we know about you lists everything we store, with the reason.

Only if you ask for it at the end of a lesson, we send one practice phishing email to the address you registered. You won't know exactly when it arrives or what it looks like; that is the test. It never asks for a password, and we only record whether its link was clicked and whether you reported it. You can pause or stop practice emails any time in Settings.

The lessons use made-up companies, people and messages. Never send real passwords, codes or bank details to anyone because of something you saw in a lesson. If you think you have been scammed, contact your bank and the police.
You can change your answers, pause or stop practice emails, and delete your account at any time in Settings. Deleting your account deletes everything we store about you.
